root_cause: Off-by-one in the length computation: n = min(src_len, dst_size) leaves no room for the terminator, so when src_len >= dst_size the write dst[n] = '\0' lands at dst[dst_size], one byte past the destination (CBMC: pointer outside object bounds in dst[n] at src/bounded_copy.c:19 with dst_size=2, src_len=3; ASan: heap-buffer-overflow in the 'truncate' test).
rationale: Copy at most dst_size - 1 bytes (dst_size >= 1 is already guaranteed by the BCOPY_ERR_SIZE check, so dst_size - 1 cannot wrap). This makes the terminator fit, yields BCOPY_TRUNCATED exactly when src_len > dst_size - 1, and keeps the self-check assertion, which now holds.
